summary: Round 2. All four round-1 findings verified fixed by independent measurement, not by reading the claim. R1: deleting each of the twelve record(...) lines in FaultInjectingStore.java in turn now refuses 12 of 12 (previously 7 of 12) -- the body-bounded brace scan is aimed at the right unit, and an unmetered verb appended at the end of the class (the presign shape) is caught with the correct line number. R3: an early return above the call and a commented-out record(...) both refuse on the REAL store, not only on the fixtures. R2: no-verbs.java exits 1 with 'lost its subject'. R4: the failure detail prints one line per missing verb. The javadoc-prose exclusion is consistent between the predicate (is_comment) and the COUNT grep, and the only direction they differ in is the safe one (predicate stricter). Hook is wired and fires: `pre-commit run check-fault-store-records --all-files` passes. No production code, no object-store request path, no cost impact. One minor recorded below.

findings.title: the predicate's exit status does not propagate -- an interpreter failure makes the gate print ok over a file it never parsed
findings.failure_scenario: MISSING=$(python3 - "$TARGET" <<'PY' ...) is a command substitution with neither `set -e` nor an explicit status check, so any non-zero exit from the embedded python leaves MISSING empty and the script falls through to the COUNT>0 branch and prints `ok 12 verb(s) metered`, exit 0. Measured: with a python3 stub on PATH that exits 127, the gate reports `ok 12 verb(s) metered` on a copy of FaultInjectingStore.java with line 577's record("stat") DELETED -- exactly the state the gate exists to refuse. The isolated trigger is not a missing interpreter (that reds check-io-seam, check-tdd and check-test-budget too, all measured exit 1, so the commit cannot land): it is any exception raised inside THIS script's 60-line inline python, which is the only gate whose predicate lives in a heredoc rather than in a scripts/*.py file the siblings share. An IndexError on an unusual brace layout, a UnicodeDecodeError, or a future-Python incompatibility greens this gate alone while every other gate stays green, re-opening the presign hole the gate was written to close and doing it silently. The repo already has the one-token convention -- check-coverage.sh:55, check-tdd.sh:15, check-test-integrity.sh:19 and check-test-budget.sh:19 all end their python call with `|| FAILED=1`; this gate is the only python-using gate that does not. Fix is `MISSING=$(python3 ... ) || { fail "the predicate did not run -- python3 exited non-zero"; finish; }`. Recorded as minor rather than major because the pre-commit path cannot actually admit a defective commit while a sibling gate is red, and because the script's two non-vacuity guards (missing file, zero @Override) close the two triggers that were predicted.
